notes: Summary: enterprise POC for Dedicated reserved GPU pools across NA + EU with multi-region failover headroom. heavy focus on throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for customer-facing chat + internal embeddings/reranking workloads.

Key requirements - throughput/latency: target sustained throughput 1,200 requests/sec peak (chat short-turn), 95th pct latency <= 120ms token-gen for primary model; embeddings 200 qps; batching acceptable for embeddings/reranking but chat latency cannot exceed SLOs.

Reserved GPU planning ask: want committed pool equivalent to 10 A100-80GB in NA primary, 6 A100-80GB in EU secondary; capacity spread across 3 AZs per region with automatic failover. ask: how to express 'equivalent' across instance types / quantized variants.
Failover headroom: require 25-35% spare capacity per region to handle AZ failover + burst (customer expects 30%). discussion point: burst credits vs permanently reserved headroom (pricing impact).

SLA negotiables: request 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool, latency SLOs tied to p95/p99 for specific API routes; negotiating SLA credits (service credits to be specified). legal wants clear incident taxonomy and MTTR commitments.

Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retention 1 year, EU data residency for EU customer data. Redwood Private considered if Dedicated can't meet data residency.

POC plan & dates: 2-week perf soak in NA (week of 2026-03-15), followed by cross-region failover test (2026-03-29). criteria: maintain p95 latency <= 120ms during 2x baseline traffic with 30% failover activation.
Metrics & telemetry: wants per-route token-level latency/cost breakdowns, per-GPU utilization dashboards, KV-cache hit rates. request retention of traces for 90 days during POC window.

Tech questions raised in meeting 2026-02-24: how Redwood calculates 'GPU equivalence' across models/quantizations; how autoscaling of Dedicated pools works w/ reserved baseline; whether can pin model versions for pools and fallback variants in a single policy.
Ops ask: network egress allocation - Glacier expects to cap outbound egress per BU and needs billing split suggestions. also wants guidance on placement groups across AZs for deterministic latency.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-10): 'We need predictable tail latencies under realistic burst scenarios - can't have 500ms spikes during market open.'
Decision criteria: predictability of tail latency, clear failover playbook, pricing transparency for reserved + burst, legal-approved SLA, and audit/security controls.

Open items: confirm per-region reserved counts after Redwood provides equivalence matrix; SLA p95/p99 numbers per route; finalize pricing for permanent 30% headroom; confirm support escalation path and 24/7 on-call for incidents affecting P1 latency.
